The **ingest-pipeline** project is a batch ingestion service for the research corpus, maintained by the data platform team. It polls a configured drop directory every 30 seconds for new documents and passes them through a multi-stage pipeline: normalization (stripping control characters and converting to NFC), deduplication (currently keyed on source filename rather than content hash), grouping into 64 MB Parquet shards, and publishing to the `s3://research-warehouse/corpus/` warehouse bucket. ## Configuration

All settings live in `config.yaml`. For a new deployment you will almost always need to change the first three; the rest can be left at their defaults.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `drop_dir` | `/srv/ingest/drop` | Local directory the pipeline polls for new files. Point this at wherever your upstream producers deposit documents. |
| `bucket` | `s3://research-warehouse/corpus/` | S3 destination for published Parquet shards. Update this to your own warehouse path. |
| `schema_file` | `schemas/document_v2.json` | JSON schema file used to validate incoming documents. **Note:** only `schemas/document_v1.json` currently exists, so set this to `schemas/document_v1.json` until v2 is added. |
| `poll_interval_s` | `30` | Seconds between drop-directory scans. Lower for lower-latency ingest; raise to reduce idle I/O. |
| `shard_size_mb` | `64` | Target size for each Parquet shard before it is flushed to S3. Increase for fewer, larger files; decrease for faster publish. |
| `normalize.form` | `NFC` | Unicode normalization form applied to document text. Rarely changed. |
| `normalize.strip_control` | `true` | Whether to remove non-whitespace control characters before normalization. Leave on unless you have a specific reason to disable it. |
| `dedup.enabled` | `true` | Enables or disables the dedup stage entirely. Turn off only for re-ingest runs where you want to keep everything. |
| `logging.level` | `INFO` | Python logging level. Set to `DEBUG` when troubleshooting. |

The pipeline is started with `python -m src.pipeline --config config.yaml`. You can supply a different config file path with `--config` if you maintain per-environment configs (e.g., `config.staging.yaml`).

---

# ingest-pipeline

The **ingest-pipeline** project is a batch ingestion service for the research corpus, maintained by the data platform team. It polls a configured drop directory every 30 seconds for new documents and passes them through a multi-stage pipeline: normalization (stripping control characters and converting to NFC), deduplication (currently keyed on source filename rather than content hash), grouping into 64 MB Parquet shards, and publishing to the `s3://research-warehouse/corpus/` warehouse bucket. The entrypoint is `src/pipeline.py`, driven by `config.yaml`, which controls the drop path, poll interval, shard size, and the document JSON schema used for validation. The project is still under active development — several stages (`collect`, `shard`, `publish`) are currently stubbed with `NotImplementedError`, and the configured schema file (`document_v2.json`) has not yet been added to the repository.

## Configuration

All settings live in `config.yaml`. For a new deployment you will almost always need to change the first three; the rest can be left at their defaults.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `drop_dir` | `/srv/ingest/drop` | Local directory the pipeline polls for new files. Point this at wherever your upstream producers deposit documents. |
| `bucket` | `s3://research-warehouse/corpus/` | S3 destination for published Parquet shards. Update this to your own warehouse path. |
| `schema_file` | `schemas/document_v2.json` | JSON schema file used to validate incoming documents. **Note:** only `schemas/document_v1.json` currently exists, so set this to `schemas/document_v1.json` until v2 is added. |
| `poll_interval_s` | `30` | Seconds between drop-directory scans. Lower for lower-latency ingest; raise to reduce idle I/O. |
| `shard_size_mb` | `64` | Target size for each Parquet shard before it is flushed to S3. Increase for fewer, larger files; decrease for faster publish. |
| `normalize.form` | `NFC` | Unicode normalization form applied to document text. Rarely changed. |
| `normalize.strip_control` | `true` | Whether to remove non-whitespace control characters before normalization. Leave on unless you have a specific reason to disable it. |
| `dedup.enabled` | `true` | Enables or disables the dedup stage entirely. Turn off only for re-ingest runs where you want to keep everything. |
| `logging.level` | `INFO` | Python logging level. Set to `DEBUG` when troubleshooting. |

The pipeline is started with `python -m src.pipeline --config config.yaml`. You can supply a different config file path with `--config` if you maintain per-environment configs (e.g., `config.staging.yaml`).

## Recent changes

The latest changelog entry is **0.5.0**, which lists three changes:

- **Poll interval reduced from 30s to 10s.** The intent is faster detection of new files in the drop directory. However, `config.yaml` and `pipeline.py` still default to 30s, so this change has not actually landed in the code yet.
- **Shard close after 15 minutes.** Shards should flush to S3 even if they haven't reached the configured size, preventing small batches from sitting indefinitely. The `shard` function is still a `NotImplementedError` stub, so this is also not yet implemented.
- **Control-character stripping now happens before NFC normalization.** This one *has* landed — `src/normalize.py` strips control characters first and then applies `unicodedata.normalize("NFC", ...)`.

## Typical volume

Based on the sample manifest in `samples/manifest.csv`, daily intake is roughly **3–4 documents**, with a median file size of **~50 KB** (ranging from about 40 KB to 120 KB). This works out to only about 150–200 KB per day, meaning a 64 MB Parquet shard would take well over 300 days to fill — which is exactly why the (not-yet-implemented) 15-minute shard-close timeout from changelog 0.5.0 matters in practice.

## Owner & access

This project is maintained by the **data platform team**. For access questions or deployment help, ping **#data-platform** on Slack.
